The firft fi-ven letters of the alphabet are commonly

muft begin and end on the fame day of the week ; and
therefore the next year will begin on the day foliow-

the dominical or Sunday letter for that year ; Then,
becaufe the next year begins on Monday, the Sunday

feventh letter G, which therefore will be the domini¬
cal letter for all that year : and as the third year will

day; therefore F will be the Sunday letter for that
year. Whence it is evident, that the Sunday letters
will go annually in a retrograde order thus, G, F, E,
D, C, B, A. And, in the courfe of leven years, if
they were all common ones, the lame days of the week

the mon'hs. But becaufe there are 366 days in a leap-

fail on the fixth of January, to which is annexed the
letter b, and not G, as in common years. By this
means, the leap-year returning every fourth year, the
order of the dominical letters is interrupted ; and the
feries cannot return to its firft ftate till after four times
feven, or 28 years ; and then the fame days of the
months return in order to the fame days of the week
as before.

The beginning of the climate is a parallel circle

It is a remarkable property of this number, that
the cards return to the order in which they were firft
placed, after a number of ftiuffles, which added to the

cards marked 3, 4, &c. never change their places is 3,
which are equal to 10, the number of the cards. This
property is not common to all numbers j the cards
fometimes returning to the firft order in a lefs number,
and fometimes in a greater number of ftiuffles than that
of the cards.
